survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses PIRLS 2021 student assessment results (reading achievement) together with student questionnaire indicators of well-being (e.g., school belonging, bullying victimization, fatigue, hunger, and absenteeism). The excerpted text does not specify whether the PIRLS 2021 complex survey design weights (and replicate weights) were applied in the analyses shown in the tables. Because PIRLS is based on a complex sampling design and reading achievement is scaled using PIRLS procedures, analysts working with the PIRLS International Database should apply the provided student sampling weights and replicate weights when estimating standard errors and confidence intervals. The report also notes that standard errors are larger for smaller groups, implying uncertainty quantification consistent with complex survey/measurement practice, but the exact weight variables are not named in the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This PIRLS Insights report is primarily descriptive and profile-based: it presents relationships between questionnaire-based well-being indicators and PIRLS reading achievement, including latent class profiles, rather than training a predictive ML model on PV-based achievement outcomes. The excerpt does not document any explicit plausible-values (PV) handling strategy (e.g., Rubin’s rules) or a missing-data procedure for the analytic tables. This is therefore treated as a reporting gap for PV/missing-data transparency in the provided text, even though PIRLS achievement scaling typically involves PVs in the underlying database.

The excerpted tables explicitly refer to the PIRLS 2021 reading assessment and student questionnaire responses; no additional grade/school-type restrictions are described in the provided text. For the latent well-being profiles, the report states that it used the five well-being indicators (school belonging, bullying victimization, fatigue, hunger, and absenteeism) to estimate four latent classes via VALR, but it does not specify any further exclusions beyond the PIRLS database standard processing.

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS Insights report uses PIRLS 2021 fourth-grade reading achievement together with student questionnaire indicators to examine how aspects of students’ well-being in school relate to reading performance. It presents country-level descriptive comparisons for five well-being indicators—school belonging, bullying victimization, fatigue on arrival, hunger on arrival, and absenteeism—showing generally higher reading scores for students reporting stronger belonging and lower bullying and absenteeism. The report also estimates four latent well-being profiles using VALR (multilevel latent class analysis) based on the five indicators, and compares their average reading achievement across countries. Across the international average, students in the “weak belonging / higher bullying / higher fatigue and hunger / more absenteeism” profiles show lower reading achievement than profiles characterized by stronger belonging and less bullying and absenteeism. The report emphasizes that PIRLS was not designed to measure well-being comprehensively and that the observed associations are not causal; it also cautions that COVID-19 may have influenced absenteeism reporting during data collection.

The report still provides substantive empirical results (table-based achievement differences and latent profile comparisons), but these are not expressed as ML model performance metrics.
